headline: Approved the Library budget FY 27-28 and the Gift Policy, both by unanimous vote.
summary: The meeting covered reports from the Friends of the Library and the Foundation, the Library Director's report on fees, daily visit data, and staffing, and committee updates. The Trustees unanimously approved the Library budget for FY 27-28 and the Gift Policy. They also unanimously approved the minutes of the September 10, 2026 meeting.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 10, 2026 meeting unanimously.
Approved the Library budget for FY 27-28 unanimously.

decision_evidence.quote: Upon a motion made by Trustee Anne LaLonde and seconded by Trustee Holly Painter, the Trustees voted unanimously to accept the minutes of the September 10, 2026 Board of Trustees Meeting.
Upon a motion made by Trustee Brenda Withey and seconded by Trustee Donna Swartwout, the Trustees voted unanimously to approve the Library budget FY 27-28.
Upon a motion made by Trustee Leslie Van Wagner and seconded by Trustee Brenda Withey, the Trustees voted unanimously to approve the Gift Policy.

plain_text:
South Burlington Library Board of Trustees  
Draft Minutes October 8, 2026 
The Library Board of Trustees held a regular meeting on October 8, 2026 at 5:30 pm, in 
the  Library Boardroom, and by Zoom.   
Members present: Whitney Kirzinger, Anne LaLonde, Ted Lenski, Christy Liddy-
Repstad, Holly Painter, Stacey Pape, Marty Reid, Rebecca Stazi, Donna Swartwout, 
Leslie Van Wagner, Brenda Withey   
Absent:  
Also present: Bree Drapa, Library Director, Merry Jones, President, Friends of the Library 
     1. Call to Order at 5:30 pm     
     2. Review of Library Exits   
     3. Comments and questions from the public not related to items on the agenda   
 None 
4. Additions and deletions to the posted agenda   
11. Strategic Plan  
5. Approve regular board minutes of September 10, 2026 Board of Trustees 
Meeting   
Upon a motion made by Trustee Anne LaLonde and seconded by Trustee Holly 
Painter, the Trustees voted unanimously to accept the minutes of the September 
10, 2026 Board of Trustees Meeting. 
6. Welcome and Chair remarks 
The Chair, Ted Lenski, expressed appreciation for the entire board's response and support 
of the library while he was away. He gave a special shout out to Anne in her role as Vice 
Chair. Ted acknowledged Bree Drapa’s one year work anniversary with SBPL. We are very 
proud to have her working at our library. Bree has brought a new perspective, motivated her 
staff and done a remarkable job in one year. Ted thanked Whitney Kirzinger, Anne LaLonde 
and Donna Swartwout for their work on the strategic plan. There is now a one page concise 
plan  for the Trustees to review. Ted shared his gratitude for all those that participated in the 
Pride Parade. It was a terrific event and the staff really felt like it was successful.  
Ted and Bree reminded the Trustees to complete the city survey regarding the budget
process. Bree shared that Brenda did a very nice job representing the library’s needs at the 
City Council meeting. 
Ted discussed the Banned Books article he had shared with all Trustees (Banned Books 
2026). He reminded the Trustees we all have a role to play in keeping all books on our 
shelves. 
7.  Friends of the South Burlington Library Report (written report submitted by Merry Jones) 
Friends of the SBPL Report for the Board of Trustees – August and September 2026 
Book Sales Total for August 2026 
Book Shop - $177.00 
Kiosk - $379.00 
Total - $571.00 
Book Shop Total for September 2026 
Book Shop - $267.00 
Kiosk - $519.46 
Total $786.46 
StoryWalk Update – We have changed out the featured book for fall to The Leaf Thief by 
Alice Hemming, a humorous book about a frantic squirrel who thinks someone is stealing the 
colorful fall leaves off his tree. One of his forest friends, Bird, explains that the leaf thief is 
actually the wind and that this is a normal cycle of nature. 
Book Sale – All hands on deck! Helpful Scouts and Friends volunteers are currently setting 
up for the sale, which will be held in the Community Room of the library on Friday, Oct. 9 
from 3:00-5:00 PM (special preview sale for Friends members), Saturday Oct. 10 and 
Sunday Oct. 11 for everyone from 10:00-2:00 PM each day. Come and shop – we have lots 
of great books of all genres for all ages at bargain prices! 
During the meeting, Merry shared that there were lots of positive comments as they were 
putting up the new StoryWalk book. It seems regardless of age, everyone is loving the new 
addition to the park.  
Merry told the Trustees that they had several Scouts and moms come and help set up the 
books for the booksale. It really made a big difference. She also acknowledged the raffle 
items are coming from Judy’s Ice Cream and The Scale Restaurant. She encouraged all 
Trustees to come to the Booksale.  
8. Foundation Report (Anne LaLonde) 
Anne shared that John Simpson, a long time library supporter and Foundation Board 
member passed away in late September. The Foundation and the Trustees acknowledged 
John’s incredible contributions to the SPBL. 
The Foundation had a Hang Out Space launch party on October 5th. The Annual Appeal is
to be sent out in early November. The Foundation received a surprise unrestricted gift of 
$5,000 from a foundation in CT. The Other Paper will have an article that illustrates how 
Foundation donations support the library. 
9. Library Director’s Report (Bree Drapa) 
Bree acknowledged the Foundation purchased milkshakes that are being delivered to the 
library staff meeting to celebrate National Library Day (celebrated on October 19) and the 
terrific job with the Koha transition. 
Bree shared the City is looking at all fees as a part of the budget process. Some library fees 
have not been increased in a few years. She is going to look at other fee structures by other 
libraries and the Board can review and discuss to see if some additional revenue/increased 
fees are appropriate.  
Nicholas Storellicastro is the new Deputy City Manager and is now Bree’s direct supervisor. 
Nicholas is taking departments located within city hall and Jessie Baker will take 
departments outside of city hall. Bree is very pleased that under Nicholas’s direction, there is 
talk of a whole building policy for a code of conduct. She will ensure that this proposed policy 
does not conflict with library policy. It is a really good first draft and very collaborative with 
others. Once the policy is approved they will work on the procedures and processes. Bree 
reminded the Trustees that only the City Manager and Deputy City Manager can trespass 
someone from the building (which includes the library). Ted and Anne will join Bree at a later 
meeting to meet Nicholas and review the MOU.  
Bree would like the next board meeting to include an agenda item for the Trustees to learn 
about S209 - civil unrest in sensitive places. She attended training and is rewriting some 
procedures that affect the library's work in the building. 
Bree shared some data about daily visits; it shows that regardless of day, there is on 
average about 50 people in the library during one hour. She indicated that on the weekends 
it is hard to get people to leave at 3 pm. The library opened for Sundays in January and the 
fact that the numbers are comparable to the other days shows the need is being met.  
 
Day Daily Average  Average/Hour 
Saturday 339.16 56.53 
Sunday 288.55 48.02 
M-F 512.23 51.2 
 Bree shared some excellent data about the library’s budget. She indicated the Trustees 
might want to consider increasing room rental fees. Quarter 4 Budget Narrative 
10.  Committee Reports   
10. A. Communications 
Holly and other members of the Communications committee shared they have a potential 
name change for when the By Laws discussion happens; they expressed appreciation to 
Stacey and others for a well done Pride Parade; tabling continues to go well with the most
Curriculum Night and Al's FrenchFries being viewed a success. There was a discussion 
about having more things to give away and some interactive activities to engage the public 
with at the table -- maybe bring some Library of Things to the event. Holly and Ted reminded 
the Trustees to check the tabling spreadsheet to sign up for future events. Tabling 
10. B. Finance 
Brenda shared the draft Library budget for the FY 27-28 fiscal year. Bree has submitted this 
draft to the City and reviewed the time line established by the City. Bree explained that while 
the budget reflects only one significant request (weekend sub), the budget process required 
her to explain each change for example, from 19- hours to 20 hours. The budget as 
presented maintains the status quo. The request for the weekend coverage is to meet the 
demands of being open on Sunday which is something the community wanted.  
It allows for some cracks to be filled by increasing some staff positions by one hour to cover 
staff meetings or training. This budget will not increase programming or other services 
offered to the community. There is one noticeable exception, the addition of hours to the 
children’s services will increase some key early literacy services. The Board and Bree have 
been sensitive to the demands of the growth of the City and still ensuring safety in staffing 
needs and meeting the growing needs of the community.  
The Trustees discussed the increase in on line and subscriptions cost compared to the cost 
of books for adults and children. Bree explained the cost of books for libraries is very 
expensive.  
Upon a motion made by Trustee Brenda Withey and seconded by Trustee Donna 
Swartwout, the Trustees voted unanimously to approve the Library budget FY 27-
28. 
     Ted expressed appreciation for Brenda’s and Bree’s work on the budget! 
10. C. Governance and Nominations 
Marty shared the Gift Policy for the Trustees to review and discuss. No concerns were 
expressed. Gift Policy 
Upon a motion made by Trustee Leslie Van Wagner and seconded by Trustee 
Brenda Withey, the Trustees voted unanimously to approve the Gift Policy. 
The discussion of the bylaws will happen at the next Governance Committee Meeting.  
11. Strategic Plan Development 
Ted expressed appreciation for the strategic plan working committee. He reminded us of the 
process from the sticky notes to 6 buckets for goals to now, this one page 4 goals document. 
He asked each Trustee to review the document for a full discussion at the next board 
meeting with the intent/hope to approve it. Ted will ask to be on the agenda for the 
November 16 CIty Council meeting to share the strategic plan.  
Some quick points by Trustees: need to add something about Collections and tie the staffing 
capacity to budgeting process.  
 
12. Other Business   
 
None
13. Adjourned at 7:02 pm. 
 
 
Respectfully submitted,   
Donna Swartwout 
Secretary, SBPL Board of Trustees
